title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. From the previous page: 𝕂 is the maximal totally real subfield of Q̄, which is Galois over Q. 𝕃 is the unique quadratic extension of 𝕂 that is Galois over Q, for example 𝕃 = 𝕂(√-1). In modern terms 𝕃 = Q^CM, the maximal CM field (the union of all CM fields).

Corollary. A subfield L ⊂ Q̄ lies in 𝕃 if and only if L is totally real, or L is a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real field. In modern terms: L is totally real or CM.

Sufficiency. This is immediate from characterization (iii) of the previous page: L ⊂ 𝕂 or L ⊂ 𝕃.

Necessity.
- Put K = L ∩ 𝕂. Since 𝕂 is Galois over Q and [𝕃:𝕂] = 2, Galois theory gives [L:K] = [L𝕂:𝕂] ∈ {1,2}.
- If [L:K] = 2, then 𝕂(L) = 𝕃. The same holds for every conjugate σL: σL ⊂ 𝕃 because 𝕃 is Galois, and σL ⊄ 𝕂 because 𝕂 is Galois.
- If some conjugate σL were real, then 𝕂(σL) = 𝕃 would be real. This is absurd, since 𝕃 contains √-1.
- Hence every embedding of L is non-real, so L is totally imaginary quadratic over the totally real K, i.e. CM.

NB. 𝕃 is the largest Galois extension of Q whose Galois group G' has the image of complex conjugation τ central. Equivalently, 𝕃 is the fixed field of the closed normal subgroup generated by the commutators [σ,τ]. Consequently 𝕃 contains Q^ab, the field of all roots of unity.

Purpose. The next page uses this to show that Weil q-numbers (|λ_α|² = Q for all conjugates) are exactly the λ ∈ 𝕃 with λλ̄ = Q. This is preparation for describing the Weil-number part of the motivic Galois group over finite fields.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor implicit steps: the use of [L:L∩𝕂] = [L𝕂:𝕂] requires that 𝕂 be Galois over Q (true, but not restated). The 'quitte à remplacer L par un conjugué' step needs σL ⊂ 𝕃 and σL ⊄ 𝕂, both of which follow from 𝕃 and 𝕂 being Galois over Q.
The NB's converse direction (any Galois M with τ central in Gal(M/Q) lies in 𝕃) is asserted without proof here. It follows from the previous page's argument.

ideas.what: Subfields of 𝕃 = 𝕂(√-1) are exactly the totally real and CM fields
ideas.modern_name: maximal CM field Q^CM; compositum of CM fields is CM
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical / folklore in CM theory (Shimura–Taniyama era); standard in Milne's and Serre's treatments of Weil numbers

ideas.what: Q^CM characterized as the largest Galois extension in which complex conjugation is central; it contains Q^ab
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; used by Serre and Milne (Weil-number torus, Langlands–Rapoport)

ideas.what: Setting up Q^CM as the home of Weil q-numbers (next page) for a Galois theory of motives over finite fields
ideas.modern_name: Weil numbers lie in Q^CM; Weil-number protorus / motivic Galois group over F_q

missed.claim: Grothendieck in 1965 explicitly isolated the maximal CM field Q^CM (as the quadratic Galois extension of the maximal totally real field) as the natural field of definition for Weil q-numbers in his 'Galois theory of motives'. This predates the published treatments by Serre, Milne and Langlands–Rapoport. The content itself is standard; only the dating is of historical interest.
missed.quote: NB 𝕃 est la plus grande extension galoisienne de ℚ telle que dans son groupe de Galois G', l'image de τ (conjugaison complexe) soit centrale.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority only, documenting early motivic thinking about Weil numbers. No new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, routine characterization of totally real and CM fields as the subfields of Q^CM. It is classical and well documented; its only interest is as early evidence of Grothendieck preparing the Weil-number side of motivic Galois theory.
transcription_corrections: The interlinear insertion likely reads something like '& qui avec 𝕂 engendre 𝕃' (i.e. L quadratic over K and generating 𝕃 together with 𝕂), not 'qui est engendrée par 𝕂'. The intended sentence is: 'on est ramené à prouver (quitte à remplacer L par un conjugué) que L est imaginaire'. The line '𝕃 ... [?] un conjugué,)' is a duplicated fragment.
In the NB, 'extension abélienne maximale de ℚ' is correct: the [?] can be removed.
First line: 'Soit L un sous-corps de ℚ̄' (the struck word precedes 'sous-corps').
